question: Technetium, the first artificially produced element used in many medical diagnostic imaging scans, is found in which group of the periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 7**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Technetium is a chemical element with the symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
 
• It is the first element to be artificially produced and is primarily used in medical diagnostic imaging scans.
 
• Technetium is found in **Group 7** of the periodic table.
 
• Elements in Group 7 are known as transition metals and share similar properties.
 
• Technetium is unique among the first 82 elements in that it has no stable isotopes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Technetium was discovered by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè in 1937.
 
• Its most common isotope, Technetium-99m, is widely used in nuclear medicine for a variety of diagnostic tests, including imaging of the heart, bones, and other organs.
 
• Technetium is produced in nuclear reactors and is a byproduct of fission in nuclear reactors and weapons.
 
• It is also used in corrosion-resistant alloys and as a tracer in hydrology.
